artifacts.summary: Class A dependency classifier now distinguishes archived-satisfied dependencies (informational) from genuinely nonexistent ones (loud), with new test coverage and synced guardrail docs.

completion_data.completion_summary: Fixed orchestrate-predispatch-review.sh's Class A false positive: dependencies satisfied by an archived task now classify as archived_satisfied (informational) instead of the loud nonexistent verdict. Added a task-lookup-lib-based archive merge, split Class A report rendering into primary/archived-satisfied lists, added 3 new test scenarios (21/21 passing), and synced the guardrail documentation's bucket enumeration. Verified live: 24 real archived-satisfied edges across this repo's active_projects[], 0 false nonexistent findings, reproduced from the deployed .claude/ copy.

memory_candidates.content: When a script that resolves task numbers against specs/state.json needs archive-awareness (a dependency, predecessor, or collision target may have been moved to specs/archive/state.json by /todo), source scripts/lib/task-lookup-lib.sh rather than hand-rolling a second archive lookup. Stage the flattened archive array to a mktemp file with a `trap 'rm -f ...' EXIT` and pass it to jq via `--slurpfile`, never `--argjson` -- a long-lived archive/state.json can exceed the OS argv/environment size limit (~960KB observed triggering exit 126 'Argument list too long'). Merge as `(active + archived) as $all`, active-first, to preserve an active-wins lookup contract when a number somehow appears in both.

When splitting a report section's findings into a demoted-but-still-visible sub-list (never suppress, only demote volume/wording), reuse an existing two-part Deferred/Admitted-style convention already present elsewhere in the same script rather than inventing a new top-level section header. Give each sub-list its own accurate '0 findings' negative so no negative message falsely implies the absence of items that only moved to the other list.
